Ganpat, a Hindu god name, derives from the Sanskrit word 'Ganapat', which means 'Lord of Ganas'. In Hindu mythology, Ganapat is known as the elephant-headed god who is the lord of beginnings, wisdom, and remover of obstacles.

Ganapat is an important figure in Hinduism, revered for his wisdom, power, and good-natured disposition. He is often invoked before starting new projects and is believed to bring success and prosperity.

The name Ganapat has a rich cultural heritage and continues to be popular among Hindus worldwide. Its origin, meaning, and significance make it a meaningful and evocative choice for those interested in the Hindu faith.
